falsifiable_hypothesis: The current target-reliable jackknife correction uses one amplitude reliability for both orientation branches. Orientation A is an auxiliary correction layered on the bagged geometry and should require variance-level confidence; orientation B is the primary calibrated branch and can use a one-step geometric confidence lift toward full jackknife correction while remaining bounded by the classical correction.
gain_rule: Reproduce shared_prior_margin_dual_gain gains exactly as in target_reliable_jackknife_theta. No gain fitting rule changes.
theta_reliability_rule: For each target compute bias_j=theta_full,j-theta_loo,j, jackknife variance v_j, and variance reliability r_j=bias_j^2/(bias_j^2+v_j), zero when numerator and denominator are both zero. Orientation A uses extra-bias confidence cA_j=r_j. Orientation B first converts r_j to amplitude reliability sqrt(r_j), then takes its geometric mean with full confidence 1, cB_j=sqrt(sqrt(r_j)). Deploy thetaA_j=theta_full,j+(1+cA_j)*bias_j and thetaB_j=theta_full,j+(1+cB_j)*bias_j. Both coefficients remain within the verified half-jackknife and full classical jackknife endpoints.
orientation_rationale: A is auxiliary and therefore retains variance-level evidence; B is the primary calibrated correction and receives exactly one geometric confidence lift. There is no exponent menu, fold/target outer routing, or outer-held rescue.

task_contract.ab_rule: average losses across separately costed A/B orientations; never average predictions
